get.summary: Manage the configuration namespaces and secrets of OpenVibe.Sources through openvibe-shared/config (D11), so the owner can give its keys and accounts on Network's Setup tab: GET /internal/config lists
get.description: **sources.config.manage** (internal): Manage the configuration namespaces and secrets of OpenVibe.Sources through openvibe-shared/config (D11), so the owner can give its keys and accounts on Network's Setup tab: GET /internal/config lists the namespace summaries, GET /internal/config/:namespace returns one as common.config-namespace@1, POST applies common.config-change@1, and PUT /internal/config/:namespace/secrets/:key sets a secret with common.config-secret-put@1 (write-only; the answer is the marker) while DELETE removes it. POST /internal/config/:namespace/test/:key asks the service's tester to try a stored value with the provider on the server, answering { ok, message } in one line that never carries a secret (the owner's Setup tab). Only Network's admin proxy, acting for the owner, holds this capability; it is never grantable to apps. Each request carries the owner as actor, and the service audits every write with that actor and key, never a secret value.

common.config-change.v1.title: ConfigChange
common.config-change.v1.description: common.config-change@1 (AI Exchange D11): body of POST /internal/config/:namespace on a service's openvibe-shared/config admin routes. It proposes a new revision of the namespace and activates it (the store validates against the namespace schema, applies env pins and calls onActivate). `merge: true` starts from the active values; otherwise `values` is the whole new set. `unset` removes keys. A secret-class key's value is never sent here: it is 422 config.secret_write_only; use common.config-secret-put@1.

values.description: The new values, one member per key. The store validates them against the namespace schema; a secret-class value here is refused.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value; a redaction marker keeps the value it stands for.

reason.description: Why the change is made; it is the revision's reason in the history.

merge.description: Merge into the active values instead of replacing them.

unset.description: Keys to remove from the new revision.

common.config-namespace.v1.title: ConfigNamespace
common.config-namespace.v1.description: common.config-namespace@1 (AI Exchange D11): one service configuration namespace as openvibe-shared/config's summary() returns it (config-pg.js), plus `sealed`, `pins` and `schema`. GET /internal/config lists these for a service and GET /internal/config/:namespace returns one. Values are the active ones over the defaults, with every secret-class value replaced by its marker; a marker never carries the value. `sealed` says whether the service has a KEK so secrets are envelopes (false is the pre-D11 plaintext behaviour). `pins` names the keys whose x-env variable is set, so their effective value is the environment's and a write is 409 config.pinned_in_env. `schema` is the namespace's JSON Schema so a client can draw the form; its annotations are title, description, x-group, x-env, x-danger, x-bind and x-unit (nano_usd, ms, bps, seconds), and for the owner's Setup tab and the clear admin panel (openvibe-shared 4.125.0) x-owner-input ({ group, unlocks, get_it_at, get_it_how, test }: a field only the owner can give), x-required-for (the feature an unset field blocks), x-enum-labels ({ value: { label, description } }), x-advanced (folded under Advanced settings) and x-example (a placeholder; never on a secret).

revision.description: The active revision; null before the namespace has one.

values.description: The active values over the defaults, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a marker, never the value.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a secret marker, and nothing else.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

sealed.description: True when the service has a KEK: secret-class values are stored as envelopes and only opened for a caller that needs them. False keeps the pre-D11 plaintext-inside-values_json behaviour, and the tab shows it in red.

pins.description: The keys whose x-env variable is set in the service process: their effective value is the environment's, read-only, and a write answers 409 config.pinned_in_env.

schema.description: The namespace's JSON Schema, or null when it has none. Annotations the client may read: title, description, x-group, x-env, x-danger, x-bind (the key whose value the secret is bound to), x-unit (nano_usd, ms, bps or seconds), x-owner-input, x-required-for, x-enum-labels, x-advanced and x-example.

active.description: The active revision as a snapshot (common.config-snapshot@1), or null.

last_known_good.description: The last revision that activated cleanly (common.config-snapshot@1), or null.

marker.description: A secret-class value, as the summary and the secret endpoints show it: never the value. The fingerprint is keyed, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key.

hint.description: The four-character hint (the value's last four characters), never more.

bound_to.description: The value of the key named by x-bind when the secret was set, e.g. a provider base_url origin.

common.config-snapshot.v1.title: ConfigSnapshot
common.config-snapshot.v1.description: One immutable revision of one service's configuration namespace (roadmap WS-C task 7; kept by openvibe-shared/config). A revision's values never change: revisions grow by one per namespace, and a rollback is a new revision that copies an older one's values. Only the state moves: proposed -> active -> superseded or rolled_back, or proposed -> rejected when validation or activation fails, in which case the previous active revision stays or is restored. A secret-class key's value never appears here: it is { redacted: true, fingerprint }, an HMAC-SHA256 of the value under a secret key the service keeps per namespace, so equal fingerprints within one namespace mean the value did not change, while the value cannot be recovered or guessed offline without that key. checksum is the sha256 of the canonical JSON (keys sorted, no whitespace) of values exactly as they appear here, secrets as their markers, so anyone can check it, and two snapshots of one namespace with the same checksum hold the same configuration.

previous_revision.description: The revision that was active when this one was proposed; null for the namespace's first.

values.description: The configuration, one member per key. A secret-class key's value is a redaction marker.

additionalProperties.description: Any JSON value. An object with a redacted member is a redaction marker, and nothing else.

fingerprint.description: HMAC-SHA256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of the value, keyed with the namespace's secret key: equal within one namespace when the value is unchanged, and not recoverable or guessable without the key.

classification.description: Every key of values, classified. A key the service does not classify is internal.

checksum.description: sha256 (hex) of the canonical JSON of values as they appear in this snapshot (secrets as their markers).

activated_at.description: When it became active; null while proposed, and for a rejected revision.

error.description: Why it was rejected: the validation errors, or what activation reported. Never a secret value.

copied_from.description: A rollback's source: the revision whose values this one copies.

common.no-body.v1.title: NoBody
common.no-body.v1.description: common.no-body@1: the capability's request carries no body; its parameters are the path and query of the routes in implementedBy (an id, a page cursor). An input schema that says so explicitly, so every active capability names one (roadmap WS-C task 4).

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

oneOf.description: AgentSubject: an agent (OpenVibe.Actor, or a developer app's agent) acting under grants its owner delegated (roadmap WS-Z2). In an event envelope, on_behalf_of names the owner.

sources.item-read-result.v1.title: SourcesItemReadResult
sources.item-read-result.v1.description: sources.item-read-result@1: answers of sources.item.read on OpenVibe.Sources. GET /api/v1/items?source=&category=&after=&limit=&include_removed= → { items, next_after, more, sources } (a change feed: items in change order, at most 500; sources gives each listed source's health); GET /api/v1/items/:id[?revisions=1] → { item, source } (the item, with its revisions when asked, and its source's health; null when the source is gone).

sources.item.v1.title: SourceItem
sources.item.v1.description: One thing a source said, with its provenance: source, canonical URL, retrieval time, content hash, raw-body hash, parser version and the terms it was ingested under. A field the source did not state is null — never guessed. Items change only through successful fetches (a new revision per content change) or an explicit, audited removal.

kind.description: article | url | sitemap | product | offer | review | review_signal | record | coupon …

identity.description: The source's own id (guid, @id, API id) or the canonical URL.

summary.description: Plain text, capped. Sources keeps metadata and short descriptions, not republishable full text.

fields.description: Adapter-specific parsed fields (offers, ratings, prices as stated, API extras).

retrieved_at.description: Last successful fetch that contained this item (observation time).

entered_by.description: Principal that entered a manual item.

sources.source-manage-result.v1.title: SourcesSourceManageResult
sources.source-manage-result.v1.description: sources.source-manage-result@1: answers of sources.source.manage on OpenVibe.Sources. POST /api/v1/sources → 201 { source }; PATCH /api/v1/sources/:key → { source } (sources.source@1 with health); DELETE /api/v1/sources/:key → 204 with no body; POST /api/v1/sources/:key/fetch → { runs } (one fetch run per endpoint; 409 for a manual source or a run in flight); POST /api/v1/sources/:key/items → { outcome, item } (201 when created); DELETE /api/v1/items/:id → { item } (the tombstoned item).

sources.source-read-result.v1.title: SourcesSourceReadResult
sources.source-read-result.v1.description: sources.source-read-result@1: answers of sources.source.read on OpenVibe.Sources. GET /api/v1/sources → { sources }; GET /api/v1/sources/:key → { source } (sources.source@1 with health); GET /api/v1/sources/:key/runs?before=&limit= → { runs, next_before } (newest first); GET /api/v1/runs?after=&source=&state=&limit= → { runs, next_after } (every source's fetch runs in order; state failed means any failure); GET /api/v1/health → { counts, attention } (sources by health status, and the failing, stale or never fetched ones).

sources.source-write-request.v1.title: SourcesSourceWriteRequest
sources.source-write-request.v1.description: sources.source-write-request@1: bodies of sources.source.manage on OpenVibe.Sources. POST /api/v1/sources registers a source (key, name, type and category required; the other sources.source@1 fields take their defaults; endpoints may be given as bare URLs; a manual source has none, any other at least one) and PATCH /api/v1/sources/:key changes one (merged over the stored source and validated again; key never changes, type not once it has items). Both refuse unknown fields. POST /api/v1/sources/:key/items adds an item to a manual source: url (the evidence) and title required. DELETE /api/v1/items/:id takes { reason } (takedown, licence, error…). DELETE /api/v1/sources/:key (only a source that never produced an item) and POST /api/v1/sources/:key/fetch take no body.

format.description: json (default), xml, tsv (a tab-separated file whose first line names the columns; BLS series files, Sources 2026-10-24) or csv (a comma-separated file with RFC 4180 quoting: a UTF-8 BOM, quoted commas, doubled quotes and line breaks inside a quoted field; USDA ERS fruit and vegetable prices, Sources 2026-11-05): the file's first line names the columns, read as an array of records keyed by those names (items_path is "").

identity_fields.description: A record's identity from several columns, joined in order with " | ", for a table where no single column is unique (USDA ERS prices a product in several forms; Sources 2026-11-05). Requires items_shape array and cannot be given with fields.identity.

duplicates.description: Two records with the same identity: first (default) keeps the first, last keeps the last in the first one's place (a file listing each series oldest to newest then yields its newest value; Sources, 2026-10-24).

items_shape.description: array (default): items_path names a JSON array of records. map: items_path names an object whose own properties are the records, in sorted key order, with the key available as the path $key (Sources#37).

where.description: Records kept only when every path equals its value (or one of an array of values), or, for { pattern }, is text the regular expression matches; others are left out before max_items counts. Paths follow the field rules: relative to the record, $key, an absolute $root.<path> into the response (a {$key} segment there is the record's map key), * for an object's single child, and key[field=value,...] selectors (Sources#39, Sources#51).

request_content_type.description: Sent as the request's Content-Type on this endpoint's GET (no body). Open Collective's GraphQL API answers a GET only with it, as its CSRF guard (Sources#65).

max_bytes.description: The body cap for this endpoint, in bytes (1 KiB to 32 MiB); the deployment's cap otherwise. OVHcloud's VPS catalog is about 12 MB (Sources#51).

extra.description: Extra fields copied as the API gave them (scalars). A path is relative to the record; $key is the map key; $root.<path> reads the response from its root, where a {$key} segment is the record's map key; * steps into an object's single child; key[field=value,...] (one to four conditions) steps into the first element of the array key whose fields equal the values, compared as text, where a value is literal text or $rec.<path> read from the record (Sources#51).

extra_lists.description: Lists the API gives (tags, job types): each field maps to a path whose array of scalars is kept as up to 20 of them; a lone scalar is a list of one and a missing value an empty list. Separate from extra, which reads an array as null (Sources, 2026-10-24).

crawl.description: type crawl only: how the crawler walks one site from its endpoints (the seeds). Every request still passes the site's robots.txt (RFC 9309) and the per-host spacing, a page that says noindex is not kept, and only what a page publishes for machines is read (schema.org JSON-LD: products and offers for deals, articles, reviews). A crawl adds pages to its frontier from the site's own sitemaps and, if asked, its links; each run fetches the pages that are due and schedules them again after recrawl_sec, so a price seen twice becomes a history.

sitemaps.description: Find pages from the site's sitemaps: the Sitemap lines of its robots.txt, else /sitemap.xml, following sitemap indexes (default true).

follow_links.description: Also follow links on crawled pages to pages of the same host that match include (default false).

include.description: Regular expressions over a URL's path and query; a page must match one (none given: every page of the host).

exclude.description: Regular expressions over a URL's path and query; a page matching one is never fetched.

max_pages.description: The most pages the frontier holds for this site (default 5000).

pages_per_run.description: Pages fetched in one run (default 100); the host spacing still applies between them.

recrawl_sec.description: How long after a fetch a page is due again (default 86400, a day).

max_depth.description: With follow_links, how many links away from a seed or sitemap page a page may be (default 2).

require_structured.description: Keep only pages that publish schema.org JSON-LD the adapter reads (default true); a page without it is fetched once and dropped from the frontier.

env.description: Name of the environment variable holding the credential. Never a value.

min_interval_ms.description: Rate limit: the least time between two requests to this source (the per-host floor and robots Crawl-delay may raise it).

retire_after_sec.description: Retire what the feed stopped showing (jobs, listings): once a fetch of this source succeeds, an item it has not seen for this many seconds is removed with reason "gone_from_source" (a change, so consumers following the change feed learn it). null (the default): items stay, as a news archive or a dataset should.

review_required.description: Products must review what they derive from this source before it can be indexable.

default_indexability.description: What a product's indexability gate starts from for content derived from this source.

search_visibility.description: members = raw items are indexed in OpenVibe.Search for staff only (never indexable).

identity.description: Stable identity within the source; the canonical URL by default.

sources.source.v1.title: Source
sources.source.v1.description: A registered source (roadmap §4.2 B, Wave 14): where it is fetched from and on what terms. Credentials are referenced by environment-variable NAME only. A source's existence is never permission to fetch: robots and terms are verified before it is enabled, and the fetcher re-checks robots.txt on every run.

format.description: json (default), xml, tsv (a tab-separated file whose first line names the columns; BLS series files, Sources 2026-10-24) or csv (a comma-separated file with RFC 4180 quoting: a UTF-8 BOM, quoted commas, doubled quotes and line breaks inside a quoted field; USDA ERS fruit and vegetable prices, Sources 2026-11-05): the file's first line names the columns, read as an array of records keyed by those names (items_path is "").

identity_fields.description: A record's identity from several columns, joined in order with " | ", for a table where no single column is unique (USDA ERS prices a product in several forms; Sources 2026-11-05). Requires items_shape array and cannot be given with fields.identity.

duplicates.description: Two records with the same identity: first (default) keeps the first, last keeps the last in the first one's place (a file listing each series oldest to newest then yields its newest value; Sources, 2026-10-24).

items_shape.description: array (default): items_path names a JSON array of records. map: items_path names an object whose own properties are the records, in sorted key order, with the key available as the path $key (Sources#37).

where.description: Records kept only when every path equals its value (or one of an array of values), or, for { pattern }, is text the regular expression matches; others are left out before max_items counts. Paths follow the field rules: relative to the record, $key, an absolute $root.<path> into the response (a {$key} segment there is the record's map key), * for an object's single child, and key[field=value,...] selectors (Sources#39, Sources#51).

request_content_type.description: Sent as the request's Content-Type on this endpoint's GET (no body). Open Collective's GraphQL API answers a GET only with it, as its CSRF guard (Sources#65).

max_bytes.description: The body cap for this endpoint, in bytes (1 KiB to 32 MiB); the deployment's cap otherwise. OVHcloud's VPS catalog is about 12 MB (Sources#51).

timeout_ms.description: This endpoint's fetch deadline, in milliseconds (1 s to 120 s); the deployment's otherwise. NYC Open Data computes the HPD per-building violation tally in 12 to 60 seconds (Sources#76).

extra.description: Extra fields copied as the API gave them (scalars). A path is relative to the record; $key is the map key; $root.<path> reads the response from its root, where a {$key} segment is the record's map key; * steps into an object's single child; key[field=value,...] (one to four conditions) steps into the first element of the array key whose fields equal the values, compared as text, where a value is literal text or $rec.<path> read from the record (Sources#51).

extra_lists.description: Lists the API gives (tags, job types): each field maps to a path whose array of scalars is kept as up to 20 of them; a lone scalar is a list of one and a missing value an empty list. Separate from extra, which reads an array as null (Sources, 2026-10-24).

extract.description: rss and atom sources only (Sources#45): facts an item states in its own title or summary, read by the source's patterns. An item that yields every REQUIRE'd field is stored as KIND with those fields; any other item is skipped. Each field's PATTERN has one capturing group; AS date turns a stated day such as October 20 into YYYY-MM-DD (without a year, the first such day on or after the item's publication).

crawl.description: type crawl only: how the crawler walks one site from its endpoints (the seeds). Every request still passes the site's robots.txt (RFC 9309) and the per-host spacing, a page that says noindex is not kept, and only what a page publishes for machines is read (schema.org JSON-LD: products and offers for deals, articles, reviews). A crawl adds pages to its frontier from the site's own sitemaps and, if asked, its links; each run fetches the pages that are due and schedules them again after recrawl_sec, so a price seen twice becomes a history.

sitemaps.description: Find pages from the site's sitemaps: the Sitemap lines of its robots.txt, else /sitemap.xml, following sitemap indexes (default true).

follow_links.description: Also follow links on crawled pages to pages of the same host that match include (default false).

include.description: Regular expressions over a URL's path and query; a page must match one (none given: every page of the host).

exclude.description: Regular expressions over a URL's path and query; a page matching one is never fetched.

max_pages.description: The most pages the frontier holds for this site (default 5000).

pages_per_run.description: Pages fetched in one run (default 100); the host spacing still applies between them.

recrawl_sec.description: How long after a fetch a page is due again (default 86400, a day).

max_depth.description: With follow_links, how many links away from a seed or sitemap page a page may be (default 2).

require_structured.description: Keep only pages that publish schema.org JSON-LD the adapter reads (default true); a page without it is fetched once and dropped from the frontier.

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
